name: Kelvex Transit Ground Filter Cap
description: A structured six-panel cap in Kelvex's standard charcoal-grey ripstop, with a stiffened brim and an integrated N95-grade filter panel across the lower face that folds down from the front brim on a snap-track. The cap's interior band is moisture-wicking synthetic terrycloth. A small Kelvex logo patch sits at the left panel in reflective orange. Ear panels are soft and unlined for comfort over long shifts.
functionality: Filter panel deploys in under two seconds, blocking particulate and light chemical vapor. Brim reduces glare in transit yards. Washable cap body; replaceable filter cartridges sold separately at Φ4 per pack of six.
what_it_says: You work somewhere that requires PPE and you've stopped thinking about it.
worn_by: Tier 2 shift workers across multiple industries
story_hooks: Kelvex caps are so ubiquitous that operatives use them as low-effort cover — but a recent batch has embedded RFID location tags that report to Kelvex HR, and workers are starting to notice.
A transit worker has worn the same Kelvex cap for six years; the reflective patch has been re-embroidered three times over with a personal symbol only her crew recognizes.
Someone is selling counterfeit Kelvex caps with the filter membrane replaced by decorative mesh — identical at a glance, useless in a fume event.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian six-panel structured cap with a pronounced stiffened brim, designed for functionality over fashion. The integrated face filter creates a distinctive dual-purpose silhouette—part transit worker gear, part respiratory protection. When filter is deployed, it reads as quasi-medical; when stowed, purely industrial.
physical_description.fit: Structured and slightly generous through the crown to accommodate shift-workers and augmented cranial ports. The ear panels are soft and unlined, designed for extended wear comfort. Adjustable rear closure (implied by transit worker standard). Filter panel sits flush against lower face when deployed.
physical_description.primary_material: Ripstop synthetic in Kelvex's proprietary charcoal-grey—durable, stain-resistant, designed for high-traffic environments. Interior band is moisture-wicking synthetic terrycloth. Filter panel is medical-grade N95 composite material.
physical_description.texture: Ripstop weave creates subtle grid pattern visible up close. Filter panel has slight mesh texture. Terrycloth interior is soft and absorbent. Brim has reinforced structure, neither floppy nor rigid.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-grey base with reflective orange Kelvex logo patch on left panel. Logo acts as both branding and low-light visibility marker.
physical_description.closures: Snap-track deployment system for filter panel (integrated magnetic or friction snaps). Likely rear velcro or plastic adjuster for head circumference.
distinctive_features: Fold-down N95 filter panel integrated into front brim on snap-track mechanism
Reflective orange Kelvex logo patch (left panel) serves as visibility marker
Soft, unlined ear panels for augmentation compatibility
Moisture-wicking terrycloth interior band for shift-worker comfort
Ripstop weave throughout for damage resistance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class). Functional gear issued or purchased by transit system employees and infrastructure workers. Not luxury, not salvage—practical corporate-adjacent.
physical_description.cultural_context: This cap signals essential worker status in the GLMZ transit infrastructure. Wearing it identifies the wearer as part of Kelvex Transit Systems' operational workforce—drivers, platform attendants, maintenance personnel. The deployed filter suggests hazard exposure (dust, particulate, air quality concerns in the industrial zones). Augmented workers appreciate the unlined ear panels for port access.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically broken-in and well-maintained by workers who depend on it. Brim may show creasing. Filter panel might have slight discoloration from use. Reflective patch remains bright (regularly replaced by Kelvex). No major wear unless belonging to a long-term veteran worker.
